what: The backfill selection SWEEP across the full admissible GHOSTREPLAY_ACCURACY_BACKFILL_BATCH domain (1..MAX_BATCH_SIZE), on a copy grown to the ENDPOINT: N_stale = SIZED_TOTAL_ROWS = 6,000, which at MIN_ADMITTED_BATCH is exactly the IMPORT_WORST_CASE_SWEEP_PAGES = 6,001 pages the import-time scan budget evaluates.
why: g-b-sweep-batch-cost froze the sweep model from a domain reaching 1,647 pages and LINEARLY EXTRAPOLATED it to 6,001. This artifact measures that endpoint on a production-shaped relation instead. Evidence for g-b-sweep-endpoint-measure.

database: gr_p2_sweep6000 -- a FRESH restore of ghostreplay-20260724T101501Z.dump (production, PostgreSQL 18.4, database 'railway', dumped 2026-07-24 03:15:01 PDT) into a local Homebrew postgresql@18 cluster on port 5433, then grown by --synthesize-sessions 6000. The restore came up as the documented fixture: alembic_version 20260720_01, 4,184 game_sessions, 131,676 session_moves, ck_game_sessions_player_accuracy convalidated.
statement: keyset SELECT_BATCH_* page: WHERE <population predicate> AND id > :last ORDER BY id LIMIT :n, swept to exhaustion; one 'sweep' = every page of one pass, so pages = ceil(N_stale / batch_size) + 1
sessions_synthesized_note: TRUE, and load-bearing. 4,354 of this copy's 8,538 game_sessions rows are CLONES of production's own ended-visible sessions -- same pgn, same player_color, same width, spread by the harness's clone projection -- because production's 1,646 ended-visible rows top out at 1,647 pages and cannot reach the endpoint. Clones carry NO session_moves rows, so this copy prices the SWEEP and nothing else: every session_moves-scaled term and the whole repair population on it are meaningless, and --derive hard-fails if it is offered as any other kind. The sweep statement reads game_sessions alone (SELECT id, player_color, pgn FROM game_sessions WHERE ...), which is why it is measured exactly here.

dimensions_before.note: POST-synthesis -- what the timed statements actually saw, and the basis this artifact's timings must stay paired with. m_total and moves_bytes are the restore's own: --synthesize-sessions adds no session_moves rows, so no timing here may be scaled by a session_moves ratio.

frozen_basis.note: max(1, 6000/8538, 10010624/14008320) = max(1, 0.7027, 0.7146) = 1. This copy is LARGER than the frozen basis on BOTH axes, so the clamp binds and its timings enter the LP undiscounted -- charging a bigger relation's cost to a smaller frozen basis, which errs in the safe direction. It is also why this copy may enter the fit at all where the fixture-scale linearity probe may not: that fixture's relation sits far BELOW the basis, so normalizing it would multiply the scan coefficient by a factor with no measurement behind it.

runs.note: Generated by --mode sweep-domain --synthesize-sessions 6000 --scan-trials 7; every trial retained. Page counts agreed across all 7 trials AND with backfill_sweep_pages at every point (agreed_sweep_pages), so each (pages, max_ms) pair comes from sweeps that walked the same domain.

endpoint.note: ceil(6000 / 1) + 1 = 6001 = ceil(SIZED_TOTAL_ROWS / MIN_ADMITTED_BATCH) + 1. The measured domain now REACHES the page count the import-time budget evaluates; nothing downstream of it is extrapolated.

effect_on_the_fit.note: The LP vertex does not move. Re-solved over this artifact AND sweep_batch_domain_20260725.json -- 34 coverage points, 22 objective -- the solution is the same a = 16170721723/677525000, b = 1414007/8200000, with the same active constraints (run B at 4 pages, run C at 824). Not one point here binds: at 6,001 pages the frozen pair models 72 x 1.0 + 518 x 6001 / 1000 = 3180.518 ms against the 3 x 1004.131 = 3012.394 ms coverage requires, a ratio of 1.056. So the shipped literals are unchanged and are now MEASURED at the endpoint rather than extrapolated to it.
